text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Monday. Prepared for Reuters by the Cooperation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Latvia's Social Democratic Labour Party held a protest action against unemployment, falling living standards, privatisation of state-owned enterprises and the cheating of depositors by commercial banks.

- The ninth session of the Baltic Assembly called on the governments of Latvia, Lithuania and Estonia to form a joint policy to further integration with NATO. The resolution on the abolition of the death penalty was not adopted because the Lithuanian delegation did not support it.
- In a telephone talk last Friday, the prime ministers of Latvia and Lithuania agreed to meet in Lithuania on October 11 over their disputed sea border.
- The Latvian security police has information that up to 40 percent of gasoline imported to Latvia is smuggled.

- Aivars Kreituss, former finance minister, and his wife Ilga, former parliament speaker, say they want to form a new faction in parliament before 1997. The two are in the political wilderness after they were dismissed from leading party, the Democratic Party Saimnieks.
- Up to 150 participants from 15 countries will take part in the international conference Banks and Finance in the Baltics '96 which will take place on October 9-11.
- Two Latvian cyclists, Viesturs Berzinsh and Ainars Kiksis, won gold medals in the European championship in Krilatskoye.
- Statoil, the state-owned Norwegian company, has decided to create a new management unit in Riga to run its operations in the Baltic states.
- On October 2, a Baltic aviation insurance pool was created including four Latvian insurance companies in Tallin.
- The advisory board of customs tariffs has asked the government to abolish export duties on round timber.
